claim: Blocks and Files reported (16 Nov 2022) that Micron had already decided a near-50% capex cut at the end of the prior quarter, and that its November 2022 announcement added further, unquantified capex cuts.
evidence: "make a near 50 percent cut in Capex spending" (decided previously); "Micron is also working toward additional capex cuts, implying more than the 50 percent already decided" (Blocks and Files, 16 Nov 2022)

claim: TrendForce News (13 Jun 2025) relayed rumors that Micron raised June 2025 DDR4 prices by 50%, and industry-source reports that some DDR4 quotes jumped as much as 100%.
evidence: "recent rumors say Micron has hiked June DDR4 prices by 50%, sending 8Gb and 16Gb spot prices soaring"; "industry sources indicate that DDR4 pricing is in chaos, with some quotes jumping as much as 100%" (TrendForce News, 13 Jun 2025)

claim: TrendForce News (3 Nov 2025), citing Commercial Times and TechNews reports, said Samsung had largely halted DRAM contract offers while other suppliers adopted a wait-and-see stance; it attributed the shift from quarterly to monthly DRAM quotes to TrendForce.
evidence: "The pricing cycle has also shifted from quarterly frameworks to monthly quotes, according to TrendForce."; "Currently, Samsung has largely halted contract offers, while other suppliers have adopted a wait-and-see stance." (TrendForce News, 3 Nov 2025; headline 'DRAM Quotes Reportedly Shift to Monthly as Samsung Largely Halts Contracts')

claim: Blocks and Files reported (25 Jun 2026) that Micron's 16 Strategic Customer Agreements represent roughly 20% of its DRAM volume and a third of its NAND volume over the agreements' terms.
evidence: "As a result, Micron has signed 16 strategic customer agreements (SCA) for memory supply, representing roughly 20 percent of its DRAM volume and a third of its NAND volume over this period." (Blocks and Files, 25 Jun 2026)
